```{python}
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from project import paths, config
from newsuse.data import DataFrame
import matplotlib as mpl
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

sns.set_style("ticks", rc=config.plotting.params)

here = paths.analyses / "valence"
modeldir = paths.glmm / "valence"

target = "event"
indexcols = [
    "country", "political", "name",
    "year", "month", "day",
]

model = f"{target}-meanfield"

def get_ppd(model: str) -> pd.Series:
    return (
        DataFrame.from_(modeldir / f"{model}-ppd.parquet")
        .assign(
            country=lambda df: df["country"].astype("category"),
            political=lambda df: df["political"].astype("category"),
            year=lambda df: df["year"].astype("int64[pyarrow]"),
            month=lambda df: df["month"].astype("int64[pyarrow]"),
            day=lambda df: df["day"].astype("int64[pyarrow]"),
            n=lambda df: df["n"].astype("int64[pyarrow]"),
        )
        .set_index([*indexcols, "n"])["ppd"]
    )
```

```{python}
data = DataFrame.from_(paths.final)
ppd = get_ppd(model)
```

```{python}
def dist(ppd: pd.Series) -> np.ndarray:
    """Posterior predictive distribution over the response
    adjusting for the quantization counts of observations.
    """
    return (
        DataFrame(np.stack(ppd.to_numpy()))
        .apply(pd.Series.value_counts, normalize=True)
        .fillna(0.0)
    )
```

# Posterior Predictive Checks

## Posterior Predictive Distribution

```{python}
ppd_overall = (
    dist(ppd)
    .pipe(lambda s: pd.concat({"overall": s}))
)
ppd_political = (
    ppd
    .groupby("political")
    .apply(dist, include_groups=False)
)
ppd_country = (
    ppd
    .groupby("country")
    .apply(dist, include_groups=False)
)
ppd_country_political = (
    ppd
    .groupby(["country", "political"])
    .apply(dist, include_groups=False)
)
```

## Observed Distribution

```{python}
obs_overall = (
    data[target]
    .value_counts(normalize=True)
    .pipe(lambda s: pd.concat({"overall": s}))
    .unstack(-1)
)
obs_political = (
    data
    .groupby("political")[target]
    .value_counts(normalize=True)
    .unstack(-1)
)
obs_country = (
    data
    .groupby("country")[target]
    .value_counts(normalize=True)
    .unstack(-1)
)
obs_country_political = (
    data
    .groupby(["country", "political"])[target]
    .value_counts(normalize=True)
    .unstack(-1)
)
```

```{python}
data_pairs = {
    "overall": (obs_overall, ppd_overall),
    "political": (obs_political, ppd_political),
    "country": (obs_country, ppd_country),
    "country_political": (obs_country_political, ppd_country_political),
}
```

## Comparison

```{python}
def plot_distributions(
    ax: mpl.axes.Axes,
    obs: pd.DataFrame,
    ppd: pd.DataFrame,
    group: str
) -> mpl.axes.Axes:
    target = obs.columns.name
    df = pd.concat(
        {
            "observed": (
                obs
                .T.rename(columns={group: "value"})
                .reset_index()
            ),
            "PPD": ppd.loc[group].T.melt(var_name=target)
        },
        names=["distribution"]
    )
    sns.barplot(
        data=df,
        y="value",
        x=target,
        hue="distribution",
        ax=ax,
    )
    ax.set_xlabel(f"{target.capitalize()} valence")
    ax.set_ylabel(None)
    return ax
```

```{python}
group = "overall"
odf, pdf = data_pairs[group]
fig, axes = plt.subplots(
    ncols=(ncols := min(3, len(odf))),
    nrows=(nrows := int(np.ceil(len(odf) / ncols))),
    figsize=(4 * ncols, 4 * nrows),
)
if isinstance(axes, mpl.axes.Axes):
    axes = np.array([[axes]])

for ax, level in zip(axes.flat, odf.index):
    plot_distributions(ax, odf.loc[[level]], pdf.loc[[level]], level)

fig.tight_layout()
```

# Ordinal prediction performance

```{python}
true = data.set_index(ppd.index.names[:-1])[target].to_numpy()
full = np.repeat(
    np.stack(ppd.to_numpy()),
    ppd.index.get_level_values("n").to_numpy(),
    axis=0,
)
mad_scores = (1 - np.abs(true[:, None] - full) / 2).mean(-1)
data["mad"] = mad_scores
data["mad"].mean()
```

```{python}
data["mad"].hist()
```
